Chapter 6: The Weight of Testimony—Carrying the Message Forward
You know, sometimes the hardest part of a life-changing experience isn’t actually making it through... it’s finding the courage to talk about it afterward.
After so many close calls with death, there’s this sense of responsibility that just keeps growing. It’s a quiet, steady pressure—knowing you’ve seen something most people never will. You feel like you have to share, even when it’s uncomfortable, or when you’re worried people might not understand.
In the weeks after the latest encounter, the world outside seemed the same as always. Grocery shopping, chatting about the weather, the constant buzz of traffic—it all kept moving, like nothing had changed. But inside? Everything was different. Suddenly, there was this urgency, this feeling that every little conversation was a chance to plant a tiny seed of hope. At the same time, the fear of being judged or seen as strange was very real.
Then, one afternoon—just sitting across from a friend over coffee—the conversation took a turn. Out of nowhere, this friend, who’s usually pretty guarded, admitted feeling lost... even scared of what might come after death. The moment just hung there, delicate and wide open. It would’ve been easy to dodge it, to offer something generic or just change the subject. But inside, something nudged me to be honest. So, I started sharing my story—not as a sermon, just as a simple, real account of what I’d experienced.
My friend listened closely, eyes wide, and for a few minutes, all the usual walls dropped away. There was no debate, no awkwardness—just this quiet acceptance that maybe, just maybe, there’s more to life than what we can see. That’s when it clicked: sharing these moments isn’t about convincing anyone. It’s about offering a glimpse of hope. Most of us are searching for meaning, even if we don’t talk about it.
Over time, talking about these experiences stopped feeling scary. It became less about fear, and more about love. Not everyone was ready to hear it, and that’s okay. But every now and then, a simple story—a gentle word—was enough to spark someone’s curiosity, or offer them comfort. The weight of testimony is real. But so is the privilege of carrying it.
In the end, this journey isn’t just about changing yourself. It’s about being a light for others, especially when they’re facing their own moments of darkness.
